heading: One address in, one hull out
lede: A public address is read as a number and seeded into the forge. The same address always yields the same ship — that determinism is the only property that makes a build worth claiming.

grid.p: The address is hashed locally with FNV-1a into a seed. It is never transmitted, and it is never signed with.
The seed picks hull, element, method, twelve slots, palette, finish, fastening and every proportion. Then the ship is drawn.
The bill of materials falls out of the drawing — strakes, frames, fastenings, seams — and the cost falls out of the bill.

note.text: One address also lays down a whole fleet: ten hulls, one per tradition, each seeded from address:index:hull so they are ten different ships rather than ten paint jobs on one. The fleet is berthed locally and costed at the current yard rates.

okFlag.text: There is no network call in the forge. The address sits in an input, is read, and is used to pick options. Closing the tab ends it.

text: How a hull is drawn deterministically from an address, entirely locally, with no network call.
